fields.meta_title: Audience Survey Questions, Built From a Prompt | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build audience survey questions for ticket buyers, readers, viewers, and visitors, and save every answer in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build Audience Survey Questions and Learn Who Shows Up
fields.hero_description: Build audience survey questions that ask who your readers, viewers, or visitors are, with every answer saved to your own database.
fields.features_heading: What Comes With Each Audience Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it from one prompt, and changes either one when you ask.
fields.feature_1:
Questions shaped by the decision you face

Describe your audience and the one decision the survey should settle. Emergent writes questions that fit both, and another prompt changes any wording, order, or choice.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer saved as a row you own

Each answer becomes a row in a database you own, tagged with the show, issue, or video you ask it to record. Next season's answers land in the same table for comparison.
fields.feature_3:
One question at a time on a phone

People who scan a QR code in a lobby or tap a link under a video get one question per screen, with large answer buttons. Nobody pinches and scrolls through a long page.
fields.feature_4:
A results page that splits by group

Emergent builds a results page with the survey: a count for each answer, plus a filter for one group, such as visitors who came with children. Ask for charts by prompt.
fields.feature_5:
Opted-in fans sent to your email tool

When someone ticks the box for updates, the app sends the address and answers to your email tool or CRM through its API. A theater can then write to musical fans alone.
fields.feature_6:
A short link on a domain you own

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the link on a lobby sign stays short. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.
fields.why_description: Emergent puts no response caps on an audience survey, so a sold-out run keeps adding answers to the same table.

fields.tab_content_1:
The poster budget goes to email

Brackett Playhouse asks every ticket buyer how they heard about the show, in a link inside the confirmation email. Of 1,180 answers across the fall season, 532 named the email list, 371 a friend, and 198 social media. Posters brought in 79. The spring poster budget goes to extra email sends instead.
fields.tab_content_2:
A school board reporter, picked by 884 readers

Each January, the Tarnbrook Gazette asks readers which local topic deserves more coverage. School board meetings drew 884 of 2,460 picks, ahead of housing at 702, restaurants at 516, and high school sports at 358. The editor now sends a reporter to every school board meeting.
fields.tab_content_3:
A basics video every Sunday for 1,710 new cooks

Low Flame Kitchen puts a survey link under its videos asking viewers how they would describe their cooking. Of 3,050 answers, 1,710 picked still learning, 1,040 comfortable, and 300 cook for a living. The channel kept its weeknight recipes and added a Sunday video on a basic skill, starting with knife work.
fields.tab_content_4:
Family tours move to Saturday, when 448 of 640 visit

A QR code at the Sparrowhill Science Center exit asks visitors who came with them and which day they visited. Of 1,020 answers, 640 came with children under 12. Filtered to those 640, the results page shows 448 Saturday visits. The center moved its family tours from Wednesday to Saturday morning.

fields.hero_prompt: Build audience survey questions for my community theater that ask who comes to its shows and why.

faq_plan.q: How do I create audience survey questions?

plan.angle: The live SERP mixes question lists (event, poll, generic survey examples) with one survey tool; none shows what an organization learns about its audience or what it changes afterward. This page treats an audience survey as the questions a theater, newsroom, video channel or museum asks the people who show up, and shows four surveys built from a prompt that each end in one decision: where to spend promotion money, which beat to staff, which series to start, which day to run tours. The how-to gives question-writing practice as plain advice, and the FAQ covers length, demographics, question types, tone, sharing, frequency and anonymity with no third-party claims.
tab_stories: Brackett Playhouse asks ticket buyers how they heard about the show; of 1,180 answers, 532 say the email list, 371 a friend, 198 social media and 79 a poster, and the poster budget moves to email.

The Tarnbrook Gazette asks readers to pick the local topic they want covered more; school board meetings lead with 884 of 2,460 picks, ahead of housing at 702, and the paper puts a reporter on every school board meeting.
Low Flame Kitchen, a cooking channel, asks viewers how they would describe their cooking; 1,710 of 3,050 say they are still learning, and the channel starts a Sunday beginner series.

Sparrowhill Science Center asks visitors who came with them and which day they visited; 640 of 1,020 came with children under 12, 448 of those 640 came on a Saturday, and the center adds Saturday morning family tours.
